newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL INTERBANK RATES LOWER ON BANK LENDING.
newsitem.headline: KL INTERBANK RATES LOWER ON BANK LENDING.

text.p: Malaysian interbank rates were lower on Monday morning due to lending by two large local banks which are also agent banks of Bank Negara Malaysia, dealers said.
"The big banks are lending on the one-month from 8.0 percent down to 7.5 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "We believe it was Negara's money."
One-month money was 7.8/9 percent on Friday.
One-week interbank rate was at 6.9/7.0 percent against 7.0 percent on Friday.
Dealers said if not for the injection of fresh funds, rates were likely to hold firm as the market was still tight.
The overnight rate, which closed at 5.8/9 percent on Friday, was expected to trade between 5.8 and 6.5 percent, they said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were slightly higher to reflect softer interbank rates.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was unchanged at 92.41, or an implied yield of 7.59 percent.
The December contract was up two points to 92.64, or 7.36 percent.
